gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180 costs $499 at BLUETTI's US store today (2026-11-14, in stock, against a $1,232 compare-at price), even though it is the only 1,000 Wh-class unit with a measured quiet-mode charging figure (about 37 dB at 1 m in Silent at about 280 W).
standout_why: I compared against three cited rival pages. The Power Station Guide noise guide gives no prices for any model and only links to Amazon. Power Station Geek's noise ratings give no prices, and their dB figures are taken under sustained load with no distance and no charging-versus-output split. Volt & Valley prices only the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 ($559 on 2026-11-13) and the Elite 30 V2. None of them prices the AC180, the Elite 100 V2 or the DELTA 3 Classic. None puts price next to measured charging noise.
decides: This backs the AC180 as the value pick for quiet overnight charging: $499 for 1,152 Wh with a measured 37 dB Silent mode. That is the same price as BLUETTI's own Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh), which only claims '30 dB under light loads' and has no charging measurement. It is $40 more than the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic ($459, 1,024 Wh), whose only noise figure is EcoFlow's claim of ≤30 dB at a 600 W output load. It does not decide DJI against Anker, because I could not open a maker or retailer price for either today.
